subject: Bakeoff: embeddings + reranker load plan & MAP (TTFT / p95 / concurrency)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@vectorly.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Proposal: Vectorly bakeoff scope + MAP for embeddings + reranker load testing

Hi Olivia / Marco,

Thanks for the sync earlier — per our conversation I've sketched a compact bakeoff plan and an associated mutual action plan (MAP) so we can get to a decision quickly. The goal: measure real-world SLA-relevant metrics for your search pipeline's embeddings + reranker endpoints and come back with a recommended serving profile.

Key bakeoff objectives:
- Measure Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and p50/p95/p99 latencies for the reranker at 1, 5, 10, 25 concurrent requests (RPS-based hold).
- Measure embeddings endpoint throughput (embeds/sec and tokens/sec) across batch sizes (1, 8, 32) and sequence lengths representative of your corpus (avg 64 tokens, 95p 256 tokens).
- Validate combined flow: embedding -> candidate retrieve -> reranker under synthetic and replay traffic to capture realistic tail behavior.
- Record memory/CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, and KV cache hit-rate where applicable.

Proposed test matrix (high level):
- Embeddings: batch sizes [1,8,32], seq lens [64,256], concurrency [1,4,8]. Measure throughput (items/sec), median/95th latency per request.
- Reranker: candidate sizes [10,100], payload tokens per doc [50-200], concurrency sweep [1,5,10,25]. Report TTFT, p50/p95/p99, and percent of requests exceeding 500ms.
- End-to-end: replay 10k user sessions from your anonymized sample at three QPS targets (10, 50, 200) to surface degradation modes.

Deliverables and timeline (MAP):
- Nov 5: Shared load plan + test harness (we provide harness + CI recipe).
- Nov 6-7: Redwood runs bakeoff in our dedicated test cluster; Vectorly support for dataset and quick validation.
- Nov 8: Results summary, recommended config (model variant, quantization, batching, routing), and commercial proposal.

Attachments: 20261105-vectorly-bakeoff-plan.xlsx (test matrix + sample harness commands).

Questions for you:
1) Can you provision a sanitized replay of ~10k sessions (S3 link) by EOD Nov 5?
2) Any hard latency SLOs we must honor (TTFT < X ms or p95 < Y ms)? You mentioned <300ms p95 for reranker in product call — confirm?

If that timeline works I will loop in Bench and Ops (Ben/Marissa) to schedule the test window.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: 20261105-vectorly-bakeoff-plan.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@vectorly.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@vectorly.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T02:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Proposal: Vectorly bakeoff scope + MAP for embeddings + reranker load testing

Thanks Connor — that looks good and aggressive (in a good way). Confirming:
- We'll push a sanitized S3 replay (10k sessions) by EOD Nov 5.
- Our internal product PO insists on p95 < 300ms for reranker in the interactive UX; the background ranking can tolerate higher.
- Candidate set: we will use top-100 retrieval for the reranker tests.

Two asks on our side before the bakeoff:
1) Can you include a single-run where the reranker is run with the quantized 8-bit variant for cost comparison?
2) Please include the memory footprint and per-request GPU time in the outputs so our infra team can map to instance types.

We will be available for quick triage Nov 6 morning.

— Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of Product, Vectorly

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@vectorly.ai>
Date: 2026-11-07T21:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Bakeoff results (draft) — embeddings + reranker load run 20261107

Team — uploading preliminary numbers from today's run (attached CSV). Highlights:
- Embeddings endpoint:
  - Batch=1, seq=64: 38 items/sec (median latency 26ms)
  - Batch=8, seq=64: 290 items/sec (median latency 18ms per item; batching overhead amortized)
  - Batch=32, seq=256: 540 items/sec (median latency 120ms per item; GPU memory near 78%)
- Reranker endpoint (non-quantized baseline):
  - Candidate size=10, concurrency=1: TTFT 42ms, p95 110ms, p99 240ms
  - Candidate size=100, concurrency=5: TTFT 58ms, p95 480ms, p99 820ms (noticeable tail at higher candidate counts)
  - Candidate size=100, concurrency=25: p95 980ms, >30% requests >1s — degradation primarily due to queuing and KV cache misses.
- Quantized-8bit reranker run:
  - Candidate size=100, concurrency=5: p95 560ms (+ ~16% vs baseline) but GPU utilization lower and approx 35% cost reduction estimate.
- End-to-end replay (10k sessions) at 50 QPS: average response time 480ms; p95 760ms; observed a spike to 1.4s during a short cache-warm period at minute 7.

Attachments: 20261107-load-results-emb-rerank.csv (per-run metrics), screenshots of dashboards included in the client PDF.

Initial recommendations:
1) For interactive UX target (p95 <300ms): use reranker with candidate size 10-20 and dedicated routing to low-latency pool, or run a smaller model variant for reranker and fall back to larger reranker asynchronously.
2) If Vectorly prioritizes cost: quantized-8bit with aggressive batching (8-32) yields ~30% cost reductions but increases p95 by ~15-25%.
3) For scale (concurrency 25+): recommend autoscale rules + increase KV cache size and warm-up steps to avoid tail amplification.

I'll prep a short client-facing summary PDF for Nov 8 review.

Ben
Benchmark Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: 20261107-load-results-emb-rerank.csv (csv)]

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@vectorly.ai>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@vectorly.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T15:45:00Z
Subject: Bakeoff debrief & MAP next steps — closing timeline

Olivia / Marco — thanks for the quick turnaround and for providing the replay corpus. Summary and next steps for the MAP to get to commercial close: 

Summary (short):
- Outcome: Baseline reranker meets interactive latency only at small candidate sizes (<=20). Quantized runs lower cost but increase tail latencies. Embeddings throughput scales well with batch size; recommend batching at 8 for interactive background mix.
- Risks: tail latency when candidate set >50 and concurrency >10; early cache warm-up causes short spikes.

Mutual Action Plan (finalized):
- Nov 9: Finalize target config (reranker candidate size, quantized vs baseline) — Product + Redwood.
- Nov 10: Procurement: Vectorly to confirm procurement lead and PO terms; Redwood to send initial SOW and draft pricing (Evelyn).
- Nov 12: Technical runbook handoff and small scale pilot in Vectorly dev VPC (2-week pilot start).
- Nov 26: Production go/no-go decision (post pilot).

Items we will deliver by Nov 10: client-facing PDF, recommended config yaml, cost delta estimates (quantized vs baseline), SOW draft. Items we need from Vectorly: signed NDA (if not already), PO contact, and production data access for pilot.

Can we get verbal signoff on the MAP items today? If yes we'll issue the SOW draft and target a PO by Nov 10.

Thanks,
Connor
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: 20261108-client-debrief.pdf (pdf)]
